newsitem.title: USA: Con Ed allowed 12.9 pct return on equity.
newsitem.headline: Con Ed allowed 12.9 pct return on equity.

text.p: Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc's deregulation settlement with state regulators allows the New York City utility to earn a return on equity of up to 12.9 percent, according to the settlement.

In contrast, Orange & Rockland Utilities Inc agreed to an 11.5 percent return on equity and Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp settled for 10.6 percent, those utilities said in announcing their agreements with the New York Public Service Commission staff.
Above those levels, all three utilities would return a portion to customers and use some to reduce stranded costs.

In Con Edison's case, the settlement calls for half of all earnings above the allowed point to go to shareholders. Half of the other 50 percent will be used to lower rates and half will be applied to Con Ed's generation plant as a depreciation expense to reduce stranded costs, its filing said.
But if the utility meets certain competition goals, shareholders will get all earnings -- no matter what the return on equity is, the filing continued.

This will happen, it said, if Con Edison sells 50 percent or more of its in-city fossil-fueled generating capacity to third parties, or if 15 percent or more of the utility's peak load is supplied by other power suppliers.
The 15 percent of Con Edison's service area peak load excludes power sales from the New York Power Authority.
